lead_scientists: Raja Ramanna, Homi N. Sethna, P. K. Iyengar
objective: Design, fabricate, and detonate a contained underground fission device for Peaceful Nuclear Explosions (PNE)
key_technologies_developed: Implosion-type plutonium core physics package, fast-neutron initiator, precision detonator timing systems
launch_or_test_platform: Underground shaft detonation at Pokhran Test Range, Thar Desert, Rajasthan
strategic_and_scientific_impact: Established India's sovereign nuclear capability and mastery of plutonium metallurgy
global_context_or_ranking: First confirmed nuclear test conducted outside the five permanent UN Security Council members

implementing_agency: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC), Pune
objective: Build an indigenous supercomputer after international sanctions blocked the export of Cray X-MP machines to India
key_technologies_developed: Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) architecture utilizing Inmos T800 transputers, parallel compiler software
strategic_and_scientific_impact: Overcame international technology transfer restrictions, securing high-performance computing power for molecular modeling and weather research
global_context_or_ranking: Second fastest supercomputer in the world at its launch price-performance tier; India's first supercomputer

achievement_name: Chandrayaan-1 Lunar Mission (Discovery of Water on Moon)
objective: Conduct high-resolution chemical, mineralogical, and photo-geological mapping of the lunar surface
key_technologies_developed: Moon Impact Probe (MIP), Terrain Mapping Camera (TMC), Deep Space Network (IDSN 32m antenna at Byalalu)
strategic_and_scientific_impact: Instruments (M3 and MIP) confirmed the presence of hydroxyl and water molecules across the lunar surface
global_context_or_ranking: Credited with the historic detection of water ice molecules across the lunar polar regolith

lead_scientists: K. Radhakrishnan, S. Arunan, Mylswamy Annadurai
objective: Demonstrate interplanetary spacecraft design, deep-space navigation, autonomous mission operations, and Martian imaging
key_technologies_developed: Autonomous onboard fault-recovery software, deep-space attitude control, Mars Color Camera (MCC)
launch_or_test_platform: PSLV-C25 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SHAR)
strategic_and_scientific_impact: Demonstrated cost-effective interplanetary mission engineering while studying Martian atmospheric escape and surface topography
global_context_or_ranking: First nation in the world to reach Martian orbit on its maiden attempt; first Asian nation to reach Mars

achievement_name: Chandrayaan-3 Lunar South Pole Soft Landing
lead_scientists: S. Somanath, P. Veeramuthuvel, S. Unnikrishnan Nair, M. Sankaran
objective: Execute a safe, autonomous soft landing on the lunar south polar region and deploy the Pragyan rover for in-situ science
key_technologies_developed: Lander Hazard Detection and Avoidance (LHDA) algorithms, throttleable 800N bi-propellant thrusters, Laser Doppler Velocimeters, APXS
launch_or_test_platform: LVM3-M4 launch vehicle; Vikram Lander touched down at 'Shiv Shakti Point'
strategic_and_scientific_impact: Carried out direct in-situ thermo-physical, plasma, and elemental analysis of south-polar lunar regolith (confirming sulfur)
global_context_or_ranking: First nation in history to soft-land a spacecraft near the lunar south pole; 4th nation to achieve a soft lunar landing
